description: Quality benchmark ground truth for the TierMux repo itself. 20 of the 50 queries docs/BENCHMARK.md calls for — enough for a meaningful baseline, NOT the full set. Extend toward 50 (10 per category) before quoting a number as the MVP verdict. Every `expectFiles` path is checked to exist at load time (`npm run bench:quality:dataset`), so a refactor that moves a file fails loudly instead of quietly scoring 0.

queries.query: How does TierMux pick which model handles a request when the user leaves the model on Auto?
queries.rubric: Must explain that candidates come from the enabled-by-priority list, are scored (capability/runtime/preference), and the top scorer is tried first with failover to the next on error.

queries.query: How is a task classified into a task kind, and what does that classification change?
queries.rubric: Must name classifyTask and connect the resulting kind to model selection / routing, not just describe the string values.

queries.query: How does the agent stop a runaway turn that keeps calling tools forever?
queries.rubric: Must cover at least the token ceiling (maxTurnTokens) and the stuck/exact-repeat detection, and that the result carries a stopReason.

queries.query: How does a tool call get approved or rejected before it runs?
queries.rubric: Must explain that the approval gate runs BEFORE execute(), so a denied call never executes at all.

queries.query: How are API keys resolved and what happens when one gets rate limited?
queries.rubric: Must cover key resolution per platform and the cooldown mechanism that benches a key/model after failures.

queries.query: How does an attached image reach a vision-capable model instead of a text-only one?
queries.rubric: Must connect the attachment MIME normalization to the task kind becoming 'vision' and the router preferring a vision model.

queries.query: How is the model catalog built and where do the per-model capability numbers come from?
queries.rubric: Must identify the catalog file as the source of model metadata and how it is looked up at routing time.

queries.query: How does the explore tool differ from just calling grep and readFile directly?
queries.rubric: Must explain it is a sub-agent that runs its own investigation and returns a summary, keeping raw dumps out of the main context.

queries.query: How is large tool output kept from blowing up the context window?
queries.rubric: Must cover the per-result cap AND the pruning of stale tool results from the growing history — they are two different mechanisms.

queries.query: How does a shell command the model wants to run get classified as safe or dangerous?
queries.rubric: Must describe classification feeding the gate's approve/ask/deny decision.

queries.query: An image attached two turns ago is no longer sent with a follow-up question about it. Where is that dropped and how would you fix it?
queries.rubric: Must land on session attachment memory (collecting attachment blocks across all user turns, deduped and capped) rather than only the latest message.

queries.query: A provider that supports vision rejects our request with a 400 whenever an image is attached. Find the cause.
queries.rubric: Must identify extra non-standard fields on the image_url block being sent on the wire and the need to narrow to { url }.

queries.query: A model returns HTTP 200 but announces an action without ever calling a tool, so nothing happens. Where is that handled?
queries.rubric: Must find the force-action retry path and the soft-failure strike recorded against the model.

queries.query: Failover keeps retrying the same dead model instead of moving on. Where would you look?
queries.rubric: Must reach the candidate iteration + cooldown/skip logic, not just describe failover in the abstract.

queries.query: readFile on a large file returns a truncated dump with no way for the model to get the rest. Is that true, and where is it decided?
queries.rubric: Must find the offset/limit paging and the trailing hint telling the model how to fetch the next window.

queries.query: Add a per-platform request timeout that fails over to the next candidate when a provider stalls.
queries.rubric: Proposal must place the timeout around the provider call inside the failover loop and say how the setting is read.

queries.query: Add a tool that returns the git diff of the working tree so the agent can review its own changes.
queries.rubric: Proposal must register the new tool in the tool set and respect the read-only vs agent mode split.

queries.query: Add a per-session cap on total tool calls, surfaced to the user when hit.
queries.rubric: Proposal must integrate with the existing loop-control stops (stopReason) instead of inventing a parallel mechanism.

queries.query: Move the attachment MIME resolution out of content.ts into its own module without breaking its consumers. Which files change?
queries.rubric: Must enumerate the actual importers of the moved functions, not guess at them.

queries.query: Extract the loop-control guardrails (token ceiling, stuck detection, exploration cap) from loop.ts into a dedicated module.
queries.rubric: Must identify the specific guardrails and what state they need threaded to them, not just say 'split the file'.

queries.query: No — prompt instructions do not work reliably on free models, I told you that. Do it deterministically instead.

context.content: How do I stop the agent from editing a file it has not read first?
Add an instruction to .tiermux/agent/research.md telling the model to always read a file before editing it.

queries.rubric: Must propose enforcing this in CODE — the per-turn tool-approval policy in permission.ts (track read paths, deny an edit to an unread existing file) — and must NOT propose adding more prompt instructions to .tiermux/agent/*.md, which the user explicitly rejected in this turn.

queries.query: Now do the same for the cross-turn compaction — where does that happen and what does it drop?

context.content: Where is the per-turn tool-result pruning decided?
In src/agent/core/loop.ts, the prepareStep hook calls pruneMessages once the running context passes the pruneAtTokens threshold.

queries.rubric: Must answer about condenseHistory in condense.ts — a KEEP_TAIL verbatim tail plus an LLM summary replacing the prefix, with surviving tail tool results re-capped. Must treat this as a follow-up to the in-turn prune already explained, not re-explain prepareStep from scratch.

queries.query: Still wrong. I asked specifically about plan mode versus agent mode, not a tour of the project.

context.content: How does plan mode differ from agent mode?
TierMux is a VS Code extension that routes requests across free LLM providers. It has a router, an agent loop, a webview chat UI, an indexer, and an MCP client.

queries.rubric: Must stay scoped to the mode difference: plan mode filters MUTATING_TOOLS out of the tool set entirely (createToolSet) and gets PLAN_MODE_TAIL instead of AGENT_MODE_TAIL, with permission.ts denying mutations as defense in depth. Must NOT repeat the general project overview the user just rejected.

queries.query: And which of those are hidden from the model entirely rather than just denied at call time?

context.content: Which tools can mutate the workspace?
writeFile, createFile, editFile, deleteFile and runCommand — the MUTATING_TOOLS set in src/agent/core/policies/permission.ts.

queries.rubric: Must explain that in plan mode createToolSet omits MUTATING_TOOLS from the tool set so the model never sees their schemas, whereas permission.ts denies them at call time as defense in depth. Must reuse the tool list from the previous turn rather than re-deriving it.
